chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Fadhl narrated from Sindiy ibn Muhammad al-Bazzaz and Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Najran from Asim ibn Humayd al-Hannat from Muhammad ibn Qays from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

He gave a ruling regarding a man whose family thought he had died or been killed, so his wife married and his concubine married. Each of them bore a child from her new husband. Then the first husband returned, or the master of the concubine returned. He ruled in that matter: 'The first husband takes his wife, for he is more entitled to her, and the master takes his concubine and her child, or he takes, with mutual consent, the price of the child.'

key_terms.قَضَى: He ruled / gave a legal verdict

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic legal ruling when a missing husband returns and finds his wife has remarried?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the complex fiqh of 'ghaybah' (presumed death), establishing that the return of the missing husband or master grants him priority in reclaiming his wife or concubine. It further clarifies the status of offspring born during the interim period, noting that the children belong to the original owner, who may choose to retain them or pay compensation (thaman) for the child, reflecting the flexible application of property rights in Shia jurisprudence.
